title: Pathwise Individual Rationality in Federated Learning: A Mechanism-Architecture Co-Design
abstract: arXiv:2609.14591v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Participation in federated learning (FL) comes at a cost. Clients trade off privacy, communication, and compute costs for potentially greater gains in model efficacy. This paper explores this tradeoff under the aegis of individual rationality (IR) versus autarky, the basic game-theoretic requirement that the federation provide utility no worse than local training. Using the above as the design target, we examine pathwise performance of FL, as a per-round bound on cumulative surplus, not just as an asymptotic equilibrium guarantee under different models of client data distribution heterogeneity. Along this path, clients can remain below their local-training baseline for hundreds of rounds. The natural remedy is to cap each client's per-round contribution so that this shortfall stays bounded, and we prove that it backfires, collapsing learning even at low-to-modest heterogeneity. translated_abstract: 参与联邦学习（FL）是有代价的。客户端需要权衡隐私、通信和计算成本，以换取模型效能上可能更大的收益。本文在个体理性（IR）与自给自足的博弈论基本要求下探讨这种权衡，即联邦所提供的效用不得劣于本地训练。以此作为设计目标，我们研究了联邦学习的路径级性能，将其视为累计盈余的每轮界限，而不仅仅是在不同客户端数据分布异质性模型下的渐近均衡保证。沿着这条路径，客户端可能在数百轮中都处于其本地训练基线之下。一种自然的补救措施是为每个客户端的每轮贡献设置上限，使这种不足保持有界，但我们证明这种做法会适得其反——即使在低至中等程度的异质性下也会导致学习崩溃。随后，我们提出了一种新颖的设计，将短期支付与……相结合（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文研究了联邦学习中路径级个体理性问题——客户端可能在数百轮内收益低于本地训练基线——证明了为客户端贡献设置上限的反直觉做法会导致学习崩溃，并提出了一种结合短期支付机制的机制-架构协同设计方案。
en_tdlr: This paper studies pathwise individual rationality in federated learning—showing clients can remain below their local-training baseline for hundreds of rounds—proves that capping per-client contributions backfires by collapsing learning, and proposes a novel mechanism-architecture co-design combining short-term payments.
